episodes.title: The Sopranos
probes: A family of wild ducks has settled in Tony's backyard pool, and he has been feeding and watching them.
Tony tries to talk his mother into moving to a nursing home, and she will not hear of it.
Newly pointed toward a psychiatrist, Tony sits in her office and admits his line of work leaves him depressed.

episodes.title: 46 Long
probes: Paulie and Big Pussy are put to work tracking down whoever stole Anthony Jr.'s teacher's car.
In session, Melfi presses Tony about aiming his anger at Livia at other people instead.

episodes.title: Denial, Anger, Acceptance
probes: Tony sits at his daughter's school choir recital and finds himself in tears during her solo.
A Jewish motel owner brings Tony in to deal with a son-in-law refusing to give up his share.
In session, Melfi asks Tony whether it bothered him to be compared to a monster.

episodes.title: Meadowlands
probes: At Tony's request, a police detective in his debt shadows Melfi through an evening out with a date.

episodes.title: College
probes: Tony drives Meadow from campus to campus on a college tour, the two of them alone on the road.
Tony and his daughter check into a roadside motel partway through their trip out of state.
With Tony away, Carmela has the parish priest over at the house and pours drinks.

episodes.title: Pax Soprana
probes: Tony complains that his medication has flattened his sex drive, and it is wearing on him.
Junior sits as guest of honor at a lavish celebration dinner with the family's capos around the table.
Melfi discovers her car has been taken away and repaired for her without her ever asking.

episodes.title: Down Neck
probes: In flashback, young Tony hides in the trunk of his father's car to see where his sister is being taken.
Tony tells Melfi how his father always took his sister along on outings and left him behind.
Tony frets to Melfi that his own genes may have corrupted his son and shaped who the boy becomes.

episodes.title: The Legend of Tennessee Moltisanti
probes: Chris keeps trying and failing to get anywhere with a mob screenplay he is writing.
Melfi and her ex-husband go back and forth over whether she ought to keep treating a certain patient.
Chris, losing patience at a bakery counter, makes a scene over being kept waiting for his order.

episodes.title: Boca
probes: Meadow's soccer coach has been offered a better job elsewhere, and is making plans to leave town.
Tony and Carmela can't resist trading sly, thinly veiled jokes at Junior's expense whenever he's around.
Junior's girlfriend has been happily bragging to her friends about his talents in bed, against his wishes.

episodes.title: A Hit Is a Hit
probes: Tony's neighbor invites him out for a round of golf, where the other men pepper him with questions about mob life.
Chris sits down with a gangster rapper who is tangled up with Hesh over unpaid royalties.
Tony tells Melfi about a boy with a cleft palate he and his childhood friends used to mock.

episodes.title: Nobody Knows Anything
probes: Paulie takes Pussy to a bath house, but Pussy stays fully dressed, blaming his high blood pressure.

episodes.title: Isabella
probes: A young Italian exchange student is house-sitting for the neighbours next door while they are away.
Tony drifts into a sunlit old-country daydream of a young woman nursing an infant.
Tony, listless and depressed, spends his days in bed, barely able to rouse himself.

episodes.title: I Dream of Jeannie Cusamano
probes: Carmela confronts the priest about his habit of getting close to lonely, 'spiritually thirsty' married women.
A storm knocks the power out at the Soprano house, so the family goes out for dinner instead.

episodes.title: Guy Walks into a Psychiatrist's Office...
probes: Janice has come to town to look after Livia, and Tony is uneasy about her interest in their mother's house.
Tony phones Melfi to let her know it is safe for her to come out of hiding.
Tony has a panic attack behind the wheel while driving.

episodes.title: Do Not Resuscitate
probes: Picketers turn up at one of Tony's construction sites, protesting that black workers aren't being given jobs.
Tony presses his uncle to make peace with Livia, telling him it's time the two of them talked.

episodes.title: Toodle-Fucking-Oo
probes: Meadow and her friends throw a party in her grandmother's empty house while the adults are away.
Melfi has a nightmare in which Tony passes out behind the wheel and crashes his car.
Melfi and Tony run into each other at a restaurant, and the encounter is painfully awkward for both.

episodes.title: Commendatori
probes: Paulie, thrilled to be visiting Italy for the first time, keeps finding that he does not fit in with the locals.
Chris talks about wanting to see Mount Vesuvius but ends up spending the whole trip in his hotel room.
Tony sits down with a Neapolitan crime family to haggle over the price of stolen cars.

episodes.title: Big Girls Don't Cry
probes: Adriana's birthday present to Chris is a place in an acting class, where he fidgets through the exercises.
Chris performs a scene from Rebel Without a Cause in front of his fellow acting students.
Furio has arrived from Naples and is settling into working life in New Jersey.

episodes.title: The Happy Wanderer
probes: Tony has taken over the running of Junior's high-stakes card game.
Meadow is preparing a duet for her school's cabaret night, hoping for a solo instead.
An old friend of Tony's from outside the life keeps pestering him to be let into the game.

episodes.title: D-Girl
probes: Adriana admits she kept a copy of Chris's screenplay and pushes him to hand it to someone in the film business.
Chris spends his days trailing a visiting Hollywood filmmaker and a woman from the movie business instead of doing his own work.

episodes.title: Full Leather Jacket
probes: Carmela asks her neighbour Jeannie whether her sister, a Georgetown alumna, might write Meadow a letter of recommendation.
Carmela turns up in person at the home of a woman she barely knows to discuss Meadow's college application.
Richie presents Tony with an old leather jacket that once belonged to a feared mobster, offering it as respect.

episodes.title: From Where to Eternity
probes: Paulie, badly rattled, sits down with a psychic who tells him the dead are keeping watch on him.
Paulie complains to his priest that all the money he has given the church ought to buy him some protection.
Carmela raises the subject of a vasectomy with Tony, worried about children turning up outside their marriage.

episodes.title: Bust Out
probes: Carmela pushes Tony to make things up to their son after he lets the boy down.
Tony's crew works a scheme on Scatino's store, and comes away with a batch of scalped airline tickets.

episodes.title: House Arrest
probes: Confined at home again, Junior gets his hand caught in the kitchen sink disposal and stays stuck there for hours.
Outside the pork store, the men step out to gawk at a car crash in the street, then carry on with their day.
Told to keep his nose clean, Tony passes the days stuck at his no-show job, bored out of his mind.

episodes.title: The Knight in White Satin Armor
probes: Tony trips on his way out of his mother's house, and her crying turns to quiet laughter.
Carmela announces she is planning three weeks in Rome with Rosalie Aprile.

episodes.title: Funhouse
probes: Tony comes down with food poisoning and lies sweating through a series of vivid, delirious fever dreams.
At his daughter's graduation party, Tony sits by himself smoking a cigar while the celebration goes on around him.
Meadow's high school graduation ceremony, where Tony notices Junior in the crowd chatting with her.

episodes.title: Mr. Ruggerio's Neighborhood
probes: Water floods the Soprano basement, the room where Tony likes to sit and talk business.
A drunken man in Tony's crew stumbles into the Soprano backyard at night and urinates in the swimming pool.
One of Tony's soldiers spends a thoroughly miserable birthday, still grieving for his twin brother.

episodes.title: Proshai, Livushka
probes: Late at night, Tony sits alone in front of the television watching the old black-and-white gangster picture The Public Enemy.
Meadow brings a new college boyfriend around to meet her parents, and his introduction to Tony goes badly.

episodes.title: Fortunate Son
probes: Chris gets a tip about a benefit concert worth robbing from the eager teenage son of his late boss.
Tony turns up at Svetlana's apartment to broker peace over his mother's records, and finds Irina staying there.
Svetlana keeps refusing to hand over Livia's old record collection, which Janice insists belongs to her.

episodes.title: Employee of the Month
probes: Jackie Aprile Jr. gets taken along on a collection run from a debtor by one of the older guys.
Rosalie Aprile has started seeing one of the crew, a loud newcomer recently arrived in Tony's orbit.

episodes.title: Another Toothpick
probes: Adriana decides she has had enough of hostessing at Artie's restaurant and gives up the job.
Driving home from a therapy appointment, Tony is pulled over and ticketed by a cop he cannot charm.
Artie, within Tony's earshot, lets slip just how attracted he has become to Adriana.

episodes.title: University
probes: Meadow's Columbia roommate is miserable at college, and Noah invites her along to spend time with the two of them.
Meadow's unhappy roommate keeps attaching herself to her and Noah in the dorm, getting in the way of his studying.
One of the young dancers at the Bada Bing has struck up a friendly, chatty rapport with Tony.

episodes.title: Second Opinion
probes: A singing Big Mouth Billy Bass is brought into the Bada Bing and mounted on the wall.
Angie says money is tight, but Tony notices a brand new Cadillac sitting in her driveway.
Carmela sits down with a different psychiatrist, an older colleague Melfi has referred her to.
Junior, worn down by chemotherapy, cannot get his surgeon to return any of his phone calls.

episodes.title: He Is Risen
probes: Tony takes a test drive with a saleswoman, sizing up a new car with her in the passenger seat.

episodes.title: The Telltale Moozadell
probes: Chris hands Adriana a nightclub of her own to run, and she renames the place "Crazy Horse."
Tony finds Jackie inside an illegal casino and takes him aside with a warning about Meadow.

episodes.title: ...To Save Us All from Satan's Power
probes: Bobby squeezes into the Santa suit for the Christmas party and makes an awkward, unconvincing job of it.
Meadow's Christmas gift to Tony is a singing rubber fish, and he fakes delight while the family laughs.
In a flashback to a Christmas years earlier, Pussy is oddly touchy about anyone handling his Santa costume.

episodes.title: Pine Barrens
probes: Paulie and Chris spend a freezing night sheltering inside an abandoned van deep in the woods.
Out among the pines, Paulie fires his gun into the air out of sheer frustration.
Tony drives out with Bobby to go looking for his two men, following a phone call for help.

episodes.title: Amour Fou
probes: Carmela, quietly frightened about her health, keeps welling up at the most ordinary, unexpected things.
Carmela unburdens herself to a priest, who tells her she may live with the money her husband brings home.

episodes.title: Army of One
probes: At the restaurant, Junior stands and sings "Core 'ngrato" while a drunken Meadow heckles him from the crowd.
In session with Melfi, Tony bitterly rails about the "putrid gene" he believes runs in his family.

episodes.title: For All Debts Public and Private
probes: In session, Tony says the only ways out of his line of work are dead or in the can.
Chris sits with his mother in her kitchen, the talk turning to his long-dead father.

episodes.title: No Show
probes: Meadow drifts around the house with no motivation, and Melfi recommends a therapist for her to Tony.
Meadow's new therapist encourages her talk of taking a year off college and travelling in Europe.

episodes.title: Christopher
probes: At a pro-Italian luncheon, the guest speaker's jabs at mobbed-up Italians leave the wives at the table insulted.
A Native American group picketing the local Columbus Day parade has Tony's crew taking the whole thing personally.
Silvio keeps grousing about disrespect toward Italians until Tony snaps at the whole idea of victimized groups.

episodes.title: The Weight
probes: Furio throws a housewarming party at his newly bought house, with guests dancing to Italian music.
Carmela goes along to look at houses with Furio, offering opinions on what he should buy.
Melfi tells Kupferberg that her son has started acting out while away at college.

episodes.title: Pie-O-My
probes: Late at night Tony sits alone in the stall with the ailing racehorse, murmuring to keep her calm.
Ralphie's racehorse keeps crossing the line first, and Tony keeps asking for a bigger share of the winnings.
Janice inserts herself into Bobby's household, warning that Junior will drop him if he stays lost in grief.

episodes.title: Everybody Hurts
probes: Tony spends the week doing uncharacteristically generous favors and kindnesses for various people in his life.

episodes.title: Watching Too Much Television
probes: A group of armed teenagers is sent to frighten the occupants out of a run-down house.
A relative of Carmela's pitches Tony on a real estate scheme he could get a piece of.

episodes.title: Mergers and Acquisitions
probes: Paulie's mother moves into a retirement community, where a clique of the other residents gives her the cold shoulder.
A portrait of Tony posing with the racehorse Pie-O-My is commissioned from a painter.
Furio flies back to Naples for his father's funeral and spends time with his uncle there.

episodes.title: Whoever Did This
probes: Tony floats an idea about pretending to be forgetful, and Junior passes it along to his trial investigator.

episodes.title: The Strong, Silent Type
probes: Paulie hangs the horse portrait in his own home, having it repainted so Tony wears a Napoleon-like uniform.
A new home nurse turns up to look after Junior, arranged through Svetlana Kirilenko.
Furio is back from Italy, and Carmela keeps inventing reasons to drop by and see him.

episodes.title: Calling All Cars
probes: Janice sits Bobby's frightened children down with an ouija board, which does nothing to calm them.
In a dream, Tony stands outside a strange house, telling someone he is there about a stonemason job.
Tony dreams of Carmela behind the wheel of Johnny Soprano's old car, with passengers in the back.

episodes.title: Eloise
probes: Carmela and Meadow get into a heated argument about the homosexual themes in Billy Budd.
Meadow's birthday dinner turns tense as the same literary argument with her mother carries on at the table.
Tony asks Carmela whether she is happy about Meadow becoming an independent woman; she pauses before answering.

episodes.title: Whitecaps
probes: Tony walks a waterfront Jersey Shore property with the family, taken with the view, and decides to buy the place.
The shore house sale is handled directly with its owner, a lawyer who has Tony sign a contract with a fee attached.
Tony has an enormous set of speakers installed on his boat.

episodes.title: Two Tonys
probes: A black bear wanders into the Sopranos' backyard, and Tony ends up out there himself, standing guard.
Four men who have spent two decades behind bars walk out on parole.
A therapy session ends with Tony storming out of Melfi's office mid-conversation.

episodes.title: Rat Pack
probes: Tony's newly released cousin says he isn't interested in the family business — he wants to train as a massage therapist.
Tony catches his recently released cousin giving massages to some of his own men, and is not pleased about it.
Out with the other mob wives, Adriana notices one of them never comes around anymore and asks Rosalie why.
Tony's cousin, home after two decades away, greets him with a crack about his weight.

episodes.title: Where's Johnny?
probes: Junior keeps needling Tony with the line that he never had the makings of a varsity athlete.
A local gardener ends up mowing Tony's and Johnny's lawns for free as part of a settlement.
Tony brings Chris along to a sit-down with the New York people, and Chris speaks out of turn.

episodes.title: All Happy Families...
probes: Told his men only laugh out of obligation, Tony tries a joke on them to see whether it lands.

episodes.title: Irregular Around the Margins
probes: Tony sits in a doctor's office having a small mole removed from his head.
Tony and Adriana end up alone together at the Crazy Horse late at night, talking easily.

episodes.title: Sentimental Education
probes: Blundetto and his Korean boss can barely stand each other, sniping back and forth while he works his shifts.
Between studying massage therapy and his day job, Blundetto is visibly worn down by the workload.

episodes.title: In Camelot
probes: Junior, still confined to the house, starts turning up at funerals for people he barely knew just to get out.
Chris brings a screenwriter he got to know in rehab along to one of the card games.
Junior tells his physician that having nothing to do with his days has left him depressed.

episodes.title: Marco Polo
probes: Tony's gift at the seventy-fifth birthday party is a Beretta shotgun, which one well-heeled guest cheerfully calls second-rate.
Carmela's mother quietly asks her to leave Tony off the guest list for Hugh's surprise birthday party.
Junior deliberately lets the details of the surprise party slip before the guest of honour is meant to know.

episodes.title: Unidentified Black Males
probes: Tony pulls strings to get Meadow's boyfriend a spot on a construction site crew.

episodes.title: Cold Cuts
probes: Tony drives out to the farm himself to oversee the tail end of the job the younger men have been doing.
Tony sits down to a family dinner at the Baccalieri house and grows irritated at how placid Janice has become.

episodes.title: The Test Dream
probes: In a dream, Tony rides a racehorse through the rooms of his own house while Carmela objects.
In a dream, Artie cheers Tony on while Tony has sex with Artie's wife.
Alone for the night, Tony checks into a suite at the Plaza Hotel in Manhattan.

episodes.title: Long Term Parking
probes: Carmela walks Tony around an empty patch of land, describing the spec house she wants to build there.
Standing at the site of her planned building project, Carmela notices Tony seems preoccupied, but he brushes her off.

episodes.title: All Due Respect
probes: Visiting Paulie's place, Tony finds the repainted portrait of himself with the horse hanging on the wall.
Paulie insists the uniformed portrait was commissioned out of genuine respect, while Tony stands there baffled and irritated.
After dumping the framed picture in a dumpster, Tony lingers, staring forlornly at his own painted face.

episodes.title: Members Only
probes: Unable to get Phil on the phone, Tony has to sit across from an imprisoned Johnny just to arrange a meeting.

episodes.title: Join the Club
probes: Away on a business trip, Tony keeps noticing a light blinking far off in the darkness outside his hotel window.
At dinner with a table of strangers, Tony talks vaguely about being in the middle of a midlife crisis.
Tony ends up carrying a briefcase and ID belonging to a travelling salesman who has exactly his face.

episodes.title: Mayham
probes: Chris strong-arms the screenwriter he met in rehab into writing a mob-slasher script to work off his gambling debt.
Chris and his writer pitch their slasher idea to Little Carmine, who hears the title they have settled on.

episodes.title: The Fleshy Part of the Thigh
Mr. & Mrs. John Sacrimoni Request...
probes: Johnny is let out of prison for a single day so he can attend his daughter's wedding.

episodes.title: Live Free or Die
probes: Meadow, interning at a law firm that handles white-collar cases, argues with Finn about how financial criminals are judged.
A man at Chris's addiction recovery meeting passes along a piece of gossip he has heard about a captain.
Vito's car breaks down out of state, leaving him to continue along a country road on foot.
In session, Tony tells Melfi his religion condemns homosexuality, yet insists people close to him deserve second chances.

episodes.title: Luxury Lounge
probes: In Los Angeles, Chris discovers a hotel gift lounge where celebrities are handed free luxury items.
Artie confronts Tony for having eaten at a rival restaurant instead of coming to Nuovo Vesuvio.
Chris flies out to the West Coast to cast actors for his mob-slasher movie.

episodes.title: Johnny Cakes
probes: A realtor corners Tony about buying a local store she wants to turn into a Jamba Juice.

episodes.title: The Ride
probes: Paulie balks at how much the church expects him to donate toward the neighborhood saint's feast.
Rides and stalls fill the street for the neighborhood saint's feast, with Paulie's crew running things.
Nucci chastises Paulie over his handling of the neighborhood feast, and he curses at her.

episodes.title: Moe n' Joe
probes: Janice tearfully thanks Tony over a house arrangement; Carmela comforts her while Tony rolls his eyes behind them.
Melfi suggests that Tony's sister may remind him of their mother, an idea he does not welcome.
Vito, settled into the small town, grows restless and bored with the routine of ordinary daily work.

episodes.title: Cold Stones
probes: Carmela travels to Paris with Rosalie, wandering the streets and marveling at the old stone architecture.
Abroad with an old friend, Carmela stands among centuries-old buildings, plainly moved by the city around her.

episodes.title: Kaisha
probes: Little Carmine plays host to a sitdown, hoping to talk the two families back toward peace.
Carmela raises the idea of hiring a private investigator to track down Adriana.

episodes.title: Soprano Home Movies
probes: Tony and Carmela drive up to Bobby and Janice's cabin in upstate New York to mark his birthday.
Janice's present is a compilation of old home movies showing Tony as a boy playing with his sisters.
The two couples spend an evening at the lake house drinking heavily and playing Monopoly.

episodes.title: Stage 5
probes: Chris's mob-slasher movie finally has its premiere, and the whole crew turns out to watch it.
Phil marks the birthday of his late brother Billy with a gathering of his own men.
At the baptism of Chris's baby daughter, he and Tony embrace, both of their expressions completely blank.

episodes.title: Remember When
probes: Tony and Paulie kill time together down in Miami, and Paulie's constant talking wears on Tony more each day.
Junior runs a gambling game with the other patients in his psychiatric facility.
Junior strikes up a friendship with a much younger, ill-tempered patient on his ward.

episodes.title: Chasing It
probes: Tony cracks one Jewish joke after another at Hesh's expense while Hesh sits with the crew.
Tony insists on paying Hesh a vig on the loan, even though Hesh never charged him interest.
Vito's widow comes to Tony asking for money so she can move her family somewhere else.

episodes.title: Walk Like a Man
probes: Chris insists he avoids the Bada Bing and Satriale's because being around the alcohol there makes him anxious.
Tony tells Melfi he had been planning to quit therapy, and blames his son's troubles on his own "rotten genes."
Paulie drives his car back and forth across Chris's front lawn, tearing the grass to shreds.

episodes.title: Kennedy and Heidi
probes: In Las Vegas, Tony takes peyote with a stripper and later watches the sun rise over red desert rock.
Tony hits a winning streak at a roulette table, laughing helplessly until he collapses on the casino floor.

episodes.title: The Second Coming
probes: In session with Melfi, Tony brings up a moment in Las Vegas when he sensed something beyond ordinary life, then drops it.

episodes.title: The Blue Comet
probes: Janice tells Tony that Junior's savings have run out and can no longer pay for his facility.

episodes.title: Made in America
probes: Waiting in a diner booth, Tony flips through the pages of a tabletop jukebox looking for a song.
A pair of Muslim men have been hanging around the Bada Bing, and Tony has taken note of them.
Janice makes a visit to the state facility where Junior is now living.
